section-17-1.TO: relate to— (a) a particular person or organisation, or (b) a single set of premises

section-17-2.FOR: a targeted interception warrant or targeted examination warrant
section-17-2.TO: relate to— (a) a group of persons who share a common purpose or who carry on, or may carry on, a particular activity; (b) more than one person or organisation, or more than one set of premises, where the conduct authorised or required by the warrant is for the purposes of a single investigation or operation; (c) testing or training activities

section-18-3.FOR: An application for the issue of a warrant under this Chapter
section-18-3.TO: only be made on behalf of an intercepting authority by a person holding office under the Crown

section-19-1.ON: an application made by or on behalf of an intercepting authority mentioned in section 18(1)(a) to (g)
section-19-1.IF: — (a) the Secretary of State considers that the warrant is necessary on grounds falling within section 20, (b) the Secretary of State considers that the conduct authorised by the warrant is proportionate to what is sought to be achieved by that conduct, (c) the Secretary of State considers that satisfactory arrangements made for the purposes of sections 53 and 54 (safeguards relating to disclosure etc.) are in force in relation to the warrant, and (d) except where the Secretary of State considers that there is an urgent need to issue the warrant, the decision to issue the warrant has been approved by a Judicial Commissioner

section-19-2.ON: an application made by or on behalf of the head of an intelligence service
section-19-2.IF: — (a) the Secretary of State considers that the warrant is necessary on grounds falling within section 20, (b) the Secretary of State considers that the conduct authorised by the warrant is proportionate to what is sought to be achieved by that conduct, (c) the Secretary of State considers that the warrant is or may be necessary to authorise the selection of relevant content for examination in breach of the prohibition in section 152(4) (prohibition on seeking to identify communications of individuals in the British Islands), and (d) except where the Secretary of State considers that there is an urgent need to issue the warrant, the decision to issue the warrant has been approved by a Judicial Commissioner

section-19-3.ON: an application made by or on behalf of an intercepting authority
section-19-3.IF: — (a) the Secretary of State considers that the warrant is necessary on grounds falling within section 20, (b) the Secretary of State considers that the conduct authorised by the warrant is proportionate to what is sought to be achieved by that conduct, (c) the Secretary of State considers that satisfactory arrangements made for the purposes of sections 53 and 54 (safeguards relating to disclosure etc.) are in force in relation to the warrant, and (d) except where the Secretary of State considers that there is an urgent need to issue the warrant, the decision to issue the warrant has been approved by a Judicial Commissioner

section-19-4.TO: issue a warrant under this section
section-19-4.IF: — (a) the application is a relevant Scottish application (see section 22), and (b) in the case of an application for a targeted interception warrant or a targeted examination warrant, the Secretary of State considers that the warrant is necessary only for the purpose of preventing or detecting serious crime

section-20-4.TO: be considered necessary as mentioned in subsection (2)(c)
section-20-4.ONLY IF: the information which it is considered necessary to obtain is information relating to the acts or intentions of persons outside the British Islands

section-20-5.TO: be considered necessary on grounds falling within this section
section-20-5.IF: it is considered necessary only for the purpose of gathering evidence for use in any legal proceedings

section-21-1.ON: an application made by or on behalf of an intercepting authority mentioned in section 18(1)(a) to (g)
section-21-1.IF: — (a) the application is a relevant Scottish application (see section 22), (b) the Scottish Ministers consider that the warrant is necessary on grounds falling within subsection (4), (c) the Scottish Ministers consider that the conduct authorised by the warrant is proportionate to what is sought to be achieved by that conduct, (d) the Scottish Ministers consider that satisfactory arrangements made for the purposes of sections 53 and 54 (safeguards relating to disclosure etc.) are in force in relation to the warrant, and (e) except where the Scottish Ministers consider that there is an urgent need to issue the warrant, the decision to issue the warrant has been approved by a Judicial Commissioner

section-21-2.ON: an application made by or on behalf of the head of an intelligence service
section-21-2.IF: — (a) the application is a relevant Scottish application, (b) the Scottish Ministers consider that the warrant is necessary on grounds falling within subsection (4), (c) the Scottish Ministers consider that the conduct authorised by the warrant is proportionate to what is sought to be achieved by that conduct, (d) the Scottish Ministers consider that the warrant is or may be necessary to authorise the selection of relevant content for examination in breach of the prohibition in section 152(4) (prohibition on seeking to identify communications of individuals in the British Islands), and (e) except where the Scottish Ministers consider that there is an urgent need to issue the warrant, the decision to issue the warrant has been approved by a Judicial Commissioner

section-21-3.ON: an application made by or on behalf of an intercepting authority
section-21-3.IF: — (a) the application is a relevant Scottish application, (b) the Scottish Ministers consider that the warrant is necessary on grounds falling within subsection (4), (c) the Scottish Ministers consider that the conduct authorised by the warrant is proportionate to what is sought to be achieved by that conduct, (d) the Scottish Ministers consider that satisfactory arrangements made for the purposes of sections 53 and 54 (safeguards relating to disclosure etc.) are in force in relation to the warrant, and (e) except where the Scottish Ministers consider that there is an urgent need to issue the warrant, the decision to issue the warrant has been approved by a Judicial Commissioner

section-21-5.TO: be considered necessary on grounds falling within subsection (4)
section-21-5.IF: it is considered necessary only for the purpose of gathering evidence for use in any legal proceedings

section-23-1.TO: review a person's conclusions as to the following matters— (a) whether the warrant is necessary on relevant grounds (see subsection (3)), and (b) whether the conduct that would be authorised by the warrant is proportionate to what is sought to be achieved by that conduct
section-23-1.IN: deciding whether to approve the person's decision to issue a warrant under this Chapter

section-23-2.TO: — (a) apply the same principles as would be applied by a court on an application for judicial review, and (b) consider the matters referred to in subsection (1) with a sufficient degree of care as to ensure that the Judicial Commissioner complies with the duties imposed by section 2 (general duties in relation to privacy)

section-23-4.TO: give a person written reasons for the refusal
section-23-4.WHERE: the Judicial Commissioner refuses to approve the person's decision to issue a warrant under this Chapter

section-23-5.TO: ask the Investigatory Powers Commissioner to decide whether to approve the decision to issue the warrant
section-23-5.WHERE: a Judicial Commissioner, other than the Investigatory Powers Commissioner, refuses to approve the person's decision to issue a warrant under this Chapter

section-24-2.FOR: The person who decided to issue the warrant
section-24-2.TO: inform a Judicial Commissioner that it has been issued

section-24-3.TO: — (a) decide whether to approve the decision to issue the warrant, and (b) notify the person of the Judicial Commissioner's decision
section-24-3.BEFORE: the end of the relevant period

section-24-4.IF: a Judicial Commissioner refuses to approve the decision to issue the warrant

section-25-2.FOR: The person to whom the warrant was addressed
section-25-2.TO: secure that anything in the process of being done under the warrant stops as soon as possible

section-25-3.TO: — (a) direct that any of the material obtained under the warrant is destroyed; (b) impose conditions as to the use or retention of any of that material; (c) in the case of a targeted examination warrant, impose conditions as to the use of any relevant content selected for examination under the warrant

section-25-4.TO: require an affected party to make representations about how the Judicial Commissioner should exercise any function under subsection (3)
have regard to any such representations made by an affected party (whether or not as a result of a requirement imposed under paragraph (a))

section-25-6.FOR: The person who decided to issue the warrant
section-25-6.TO: ask the Investigatory Powers Commissioner to review a decision made by any other Judicial Commissioner under subsection (3)

section-25-7.TO: — (a) confirm the Judicial Commissioner's decision, or (b) make a fresh determination

section-26-2.TO: issue the warrant without the approval of (a) the Prime Minister, or (b) if conditions A and B are met, an individual (other than that Secretary of State) designated by the Prime Minister under this section

section-26-2C.TO: designate up to five individuals under this section

section-26-2D.TO: designate an individual under this section
section-26-2D.ONLY IF: the individual— (a) holds the office of Secretary of State, and (b) has the necessary operational awareness to decide whether to give approvals under subsection (2)

section-27-2.TO: contain a statement that the purpose, or one of the purposes, of the warrant is to authorise or require the interception, or (in the case of a targeted examination warrant) the selection for examination, of items subject to legal privilege

section-27-3.FOR: the person to whom the application is made
section-27-3.TO: have regard to the public interest in the confidentiality of items subject to legal privilege
section-27-3.IN: deciding whether to issue the warrant

section-27-4.FOR: The person to whom the application is made
section-27-4.ONLY IF: the person considers— (a) that there are exceptional and compelling circumstances that make it necessary to authorise or require the interception, or (in the case of a targeted examination warrant) the selection for examination, of items subject to legal privilege, and (b) that the arrangements made for the purposes of section 53 or (as the case may be) section 150 (safeguards relating to retention and disclosure of material) include specific arrangements for the handling, retention, use and destruction of such items

section-27-5.IF: it is considered necessary only as mentioned in section 20(2)(c)

section-27-8.TO: contain— (a) a statement that the intercepting authority considers that the relevant communications are likely to include items subject to legal privilege, and (b) an assessment of how likely it is that the relevant communications will include such items

section-27-9.FOR: The person to whom the application is made
section-27-9.ONLY IF: the person considers that the arrangements made for the purposes of section 53 or (as the case may be) section 150 include specific arrangements for the handling, retention, use and destruction of items subject to legal privilege

section-27-12.TO: — (a) contain a statement that the purpose, or one of the purposes, of the warrant is to authorise or require the interception, or (in the case of a targeted examination warrant) the selection for examination, of communications that, if they were not made with the intention of furthering a criminal purpose, would be items subject to legal privilege, and (b) set out the reasons for believing that the targeted communications are likely to be communications made with the intention of furthering a criminal purpose

section-27-13.FOR: The person to whom the application is made
section-27-13.ONLY IF: the person considers that the targeted communications are likely to be communications made with the intention of furthering a criminal purpose

section-28-2.TO: contain a statement that the purpose, or one of the purposes, of the warrant is— (a) in the case of a targeted interception warrant or mutual assistance warrant, to authorise or require the interception of communications which the intercepting authority believes will be communications containing confidential journalistic material, or (b) in the case of a targeted examination warrant, to authorise the selection for examination of journalistic material which the intercepting authority believes is confidential journalistic material

section-28-3.FOR: The person to whom the application is made
section-28-3.ONLY IF: the person considers that the arrangements made for the purposes of section 53 or (as the case may be) section 150 (safeguards relating to retention and disclosure of material) include specific arrangements for the handling, retention, use and destruction of communications containing confidential journalistic material

section-29-2.TO: contain a statement that the purpose, or one of the purposes, of the warrant is to identify or confirm a source of journalistic information

section-29-3.FOR: The person to whom the application is made
section-29-3.ONLY IF: the person considers that the arrangements made for the purposes of section 53 or (as the case may be) section 150 (safeguards relating to retention and disclosure of material) include specific arrangements for the handling, retention, use and destruction of communications that identify sources of journalistic information

section-30-1.FOR: The decision to issue a warrant under this Chapter
section-30-1.TO: be taken personally by— (a) the Secretary of State, or (b) in the case of a warrant to be issued by the Scottish Ministers, a member of the Scottish Government
section-30-1.SUBJECT TO: — (a) subsection (4), and (b) section 40 (special rules for certain mutual assistance warrants)

section-30-2.TO: be signed by the person who has taken the decision to issue it
section-30-2.SUBJECT TO: — (a) subsection (4), and (b) section 40 (special rules for certain mutual assistance warrants)

section-30-4.TO: be signed by a senior official designated by the Secretary of State or (as the case may be) the Scottish Ministers for that purpose
section-30-4.IF: it is not reasonably practicable for a warrant to be signed by the person who has taken the decision to issue it

section-30-5.TO: contain a statement that— (a) it is not reasonably practicable for the warrant to be signed by the person who took the decision to issue it, and (b) the Secretary of State or (as the case may be) a member of the Scottish Government has personally and expressly authorised the issue of the warrant

section-31-1.TO: contain a provision stating whether it is a targeted interception warrant, a targeted examination warrant or a mutual assistance warrant

section-31-2.FOR: a warrant issued under this Chapter
section-31-2.TO: be addressed to the person by whom, or on whose behalf, the application for the warrant was made

section-31-3.FOR: A warrant that relates to a particular person or organisation, or to a single set of premises
section-31-3.TO: name or describe that person or organisation or those premises

section-31-4.FOR: A warrant that relates to a group of persons who share a common purpose or who carry on (or may carry on) a particular activity
section-31-4.TO: — (a) describe that purpose or activity, and (b) name or describe as many of those persons as it is reasonably practicable to name or describe

section-31-5.FOR: A warrant that relates to more than one person or organisation, or more than one set of premises, where the conduct authorised or required by the warrant is for the purposes of a single investigation or operation
section-31-5.TO: — (a) describe the investigation or operation, and (b) name or describe as many of those persons or organisations, or as many of those sets of premises, as it is reasonably practicable to name or describe

section-31-6.FOR: A warrant that relates to any testing or training activities
section-31-6.TO: — (a) describe those activities, and (b) name or describe as many of the persons within subsection (7) as it is reasonably practicable to name or describe

section-31-8.FOR: a targeted interception warrant or mutual assistance warrant or a targeted examination warrant
section-31-8.TO: specify the addresses, numbers, apparatus, or other factors, or combination of factors, that are to be used for identifying the communications
section-31-8.WHERE: Where— (a) the targeted interception warrant or mutual assistance warrant authorises or requires the interception of communications described in the warrant, or the obtaining of secondary data from such communications, or (b) the targeted examination warrant authorises the selection of the content of communications for examination

section-31-9.FOR: Any factor, or combination of factors, specified in accordance with subsection (8)
section-31-9.TO: be one that identifies communications which are likely to be or to include— (a) communications from, or intended for, any person or organisation named or described in the warrant, or (b) communications originating on, or intended for transmission to, any premises named or described in the warrant

section-33-1.FOR: a warrant issued under this Chapter
section-33-1.TO: be renewed by an instrument issued by the appropriate person (see subsection (3))
section-33-1.AT: any time during the renewal period
section-33-1.SUBJECT TO: section 40 (special rules for certain mutual assistance warrants)

section-33-6.FOR: The decision to renew a warrant
section-33-6.TO: be taken personally by the appropriate person
section-33-6.SUBJECT TO: section 40 (special rules for certain mutual assistance warrants)
section 40 (special rules for certain mutual assistance warrants)

section-34-1.FOR: the provisions of a warrant issued under this Chapter
section-34-1.TO: be modified by an instrument issued by the person making the modification

section-34-3.TO: be modified as mentioned in subsection (2)(a)
section-34-3.IF: it relates only to a particular person or organisation, or to a single set of premises, as mentioned in section 17(1)

section-34-4.FOR: The decision to modify the provisions of a warrant
section-34-4.TO: be taken personally by the person making the modification

section-35-1.FOR: — (a) the Secretary of State, in the case of a warrant issued by the Secretary of State, (b) a member of the Scottish Government, in the case of a warrant issued by the Scottish Ministers, or (c) a senior official acting on behalf of the Secretary of State or (as the case may be) the Scottish Ministers
section-35-1.SUBJECT TO: section 36(5) and (6) (special rules where any of sections 26 to 29 applies in relation to the making of a major modification)

section-35-2.FOR: — (a) the Secretary of State, in the case of a warrant issued by the Secretary of State, (b) a member of the Scottish Government, in the case of a warrant issued by the Scottish Ministers, (c) a senior official acting on behalf of the Secretary of State or (as the case may be) the Scottish Ministers, (d) the person to whom the warrant is addressed, or (e) a person who holds a senior position in the same public authority as the person mentioned in paragraph (d)

section-35-3.IF: that person considers that there is an urgent need to do so
section-35-3.SUBJECT TO: section 36(5) and (6) (special rules where any of sections 26 to 29 applies in relation to the making of a major modification)
section-35-3.EXCEPT: in the case of a mutual assistance warrant addressed to a person falling within section 18(1)(h) (competent authorities of overseas countries or territories)

section-36-1.ONLY IF: the person considers— (a) that the modification is necessary on any relevant grounds (see subsection (3)), and (b) that the conduct authorised by the modification is proportionate to what is sought to be achieved by that conduct

section-36-5.TO: be made by the Secretary of State
section-36-5.WHERE: section 26 applies in relation to the making of the modification

section-36-6.TO: be made by— (i) the Secretary of State or (in the case of a warrant issued by the Scottish Ministers) a member of the Scottish Government, or (ii) if a senior official acting on behalf of a person within sub-paragraph (i) considers that there is an urgent need to make the modification, that senior official
section-36-6.WHERE: section 27, 28 or 29 applies in relation to the making of the modification

section-36-8.TO: be signed by a senior official designated by the Secretary of State or (as the case may be) the Scottish Ministers for that purpose
section-36-8.IF: it is not reasonably practicable for the instrument to be signed by the Secretary of State or (as the case may be) a member of the Scottish Government in accordance with section 34(4)
section-36-8.IN: a case where any of sections 26 to 29 applies in relation to the making of a major modification

section-36-9.TO: contain a statement that— (a) it is not reasonably practicable for the instrument to be signed by the person who took the decision to make the modification, and (b) the Secretary of State or (as the case may be) a member of the Scottish Government has personally and expressly authorised the making of the modification

section-36-10.TO: modify the warrant by removing that factor
section-36-10.IF: at any time the person considers that any factor specified in a warrant in accordance with section 31(8) is no longer relevant for identifying communications which, in the case of that warrant, are likely to be, or to include, communications falling within section 31(9)(a) or (b)

section-37-1.TO: be notified of a major modification of a warrant under this Chapter and the reasons for making it
section-37-1.AS SOON AS: is reasonably practicable after the person makes the modification
section-37-1.UNLESS: (a) the modification is made by virtue of section 35(3), or (b) any of sections 26 to 29 applies in relation to the making of the modification

section-37-3.FOR: the Secretary of State or (in the case of a warrant issued by the Scottish Ministers) a member of the Scottish Government
section-37-3.TO: be notified personally of a major modification and the reasons for making it
section-37-3.WHERE: the modification is made by a senior official in accordance with section 35(1) or section 36(6)(a)(ii)

section-38-3.FOR: The person who made the modification
section-38-3.TO: inform the appropriate person that it has been made

section-38-5.TO: — (a) decide whether to approve the decision to make the modification, and (b) notify the person of the appropriate person's decision
section-38-5.BEFORE: the end of the relevant period

section-38-6.TO: be notified of a decision under subsection (5)
section-38-6.AS SOON AS: reasonably practicable after a designated senior official makes the decision

section-38-6.IF: the senior official has decided to approve the decision to make the modification
section-38-6.AS SOON AS: reasonably practicable after a designated senior official makes the decision

section-38-6.FOR: the Secretary of State or (in the case of a warrant issued by the Scottish Ministers) a member of the Scottish Government
section-38-6.TO: be notified personally of the matters mentioned in paragraph (a)(i) and (ii)
section-38-6.AS SOON AS: reasonably practicable after a designated senior official makes a decision under subsection (5)

section-38-7.FOR: the person to whom the warrant is addressed
section-38-7.TO: secure that anything in the process of being done under the warrant by virtue of that modification stops as soon as possible
section-38-7.IF: the appropriate person refuses to approve the decision to make the modification

section-39-1.TO: cancel a warrant issued under this Chapter

section-39-2.TO: cancel a warrant issued under this Chapter
section-39-2.IF: the person considers that— (a) the warrant is no longer necessary on any relevant grounds, or (b) the conduct authorised by the warrant is no longer proportionate to what is sought to be achieved by that conduct

section-39-5.FOR: the person to whom a warrant was addressed
section-39-5.TO: secure that anything in the process of being done under the warrant stops as soon as possible
section-39-5.WHERE: the warrant is cancelled under this section

section-39-6.FOR: a warrant that has been cancelled under this section

section-40-2.FOR: a senior official designated by the Secretary of State for that purpose
section-40-2.TO: take the decision to issue a relevant mutual assistance warrant

section-40-3.TO: contain— (a) a statement that the warrant is issued for the purposes of a request for assistance made under an international mutual assistance agreement by the competent authorities of a country or territory outside the United Kingdom, and (b) whichever of the following statements is applicable— (i) a statement that the interception subject appears to be outside the United Kingdom; (ii) a statement that the interception authorised or required by the warrant is to take place in relation only to premises outside the United Kingdom

section-40-4.FOR: a senior official designated by the Secretary of State for that purpose
section-40-4.TO: renew a relevant mutual assistance warrant

section-40-5.TO: contain— (a) a statement that the renewal is for the purposes of a request for assistance made under an international mutual assistance agreement by the competent authorities of a country or territory outside the United Kingdom, and (b) whichever of the following statements is applicable— (i) a statement that the interception subject appears to be outside the United Kingdom; (ii) a statement that the interception authorised or required by the warrant is to take place in relation only to premises outside the United Kingdom
section-40-5.WHERE: a senior official renews a relevant mutual assistance warrant in accordance with subsection (4)

section-40-7.FOR: the Secretary of State, or a senior official acting on behalf of the Secretary of State
section-40-7.IF: that person believes that the person, group or organisation named or described in the warrant as the interception subject is in the United Kingdom

section-41-2.FOR: the person to whom a warrant to which this section applies is addressed (“the intercepting authority”)
section-41-2.TO: (in addition to acting alone) act through, or together with, such other persons as the intercepting authority may require (whether under subsection (3) or otherwise) to provide the authority with assistance in giving effect to the warrant

section-41-3.TO: For the purpose of requiring any person to provide assistance in relation to a warrant to which this section applies, — (a) serve a copy of the warrant on any person who the intercepting authority considers may be able to provide such assistance, or (b) make arrangements for the service of a copy of the warrant on any such person

section-41-4.TO: be served under subsection (3) on a person outside the United Kingdom for the purpose of requiring the person to provide such assistance in the form of conduct outside the United Kingdom

section-42-2.TO: be served in such a way as to bring the contents of the warrant to the attention of the person who the intercepting authority considers may be able to provide assistance in relation to it

section-42-3.TO: be served on a person outside the United Kingdom in any of the following ways (as well as by electronic or other means of service)— (a) by serving it at the person's principal office within the United Kingdom or, if the person has no such office in the United Kingdom, at any place in the United Kingdom where the person carries on business or conducts activities; (b) if the person has specified an address in the United Kingdom as one at which the person, or someone on the person's behalf, will accept service of documents of the same description as a copy of a warrant, by serving it at that address; (c) by making it available for inspection (whether to the person or to someone acting on the person's behalf) at a place in the United Kingdom

section-42-4.TO: be served on a person outside the United Kingdom in the way mentioned in subsection (3)(c)
section-42-4.ONLY IF: — (a) it is not reasonably practicable for a copy to be served by any other means (whether as mentioned in subsection (3)(a) or (b) or otherwise), and (b) the intercepting authority takes such steps as the authority considers appropriate for the purpose of bringing the contents of the warrant, and the availability of a copy for inspection, to the attention of the person

section-42-5.AS SOON AS: reasonably practicable after the copy of the warrant is made available for inspection

section-43-1.FOR: A relevant operator that has been served with a copy of a warrant to which section 41 applies by (or on behalf of) the intercepting authority
section-43-1.TO: take all steps for giving effect to the warrant that are notified to the relevant operator by (or on behalf of) the intercepting authority

section-43-4.TO: take any steps which it is not reasonably practicable for the relevant operator to take

section-43-7.TO: knowingly fail to comply with subsection (1)

section-46-2.TO: by regulations authorise conduct of a description specified in the regulations
section-46-2.IF: that conduct appears to the Secretary of State to constitute a legitimate practice reasonably required for the purpose, in connection with the carrying on of any relevant activities (see subsection (4)), of monitoring or keeping a record of— (a) communications by means of which transactions are entered into in the course of the relevant activities, or (b) other communications relating to the relevant activities or taking place in the course of the carrying on of those activities

section-46-3.TO: authorise the interception of any communication except in the course of its transmission using apparatus or services provided by or to the person carrying on the relevant activities for use (whether wholly or partly) in connection with those activities

section-52-7.TO: designate the agreement as a relevant international agreement
section-52-7.UNLESS: the Secretary of State has sought, in respect of each country or territory referred to in subsection (6), a written assurance, or written assurances, relating to the non-use of information obtained by virtue of the agreement in connection with proceedings for a death penalty offence in the country or territory

section-53-1.TO: ensure, in relation to every targeted interception warrant or mutual assistance warrant issued by that authority, that arrangements are in force for securing that the requirements of subsections (2) and (5) are met in relation to the material obtained under the warrant

section-53-7.FOR: the person to whom the warrant is addressed
section-53-7.WHERE: — (a) a communication which has been intercepted in accordance with a targeted interception warrant or mutual assistance warrant is retained, following its examination, for purposes other than the destruction of the communication, and (b) it is a communication that contains confidential journalistic material or identifies a source of journalistic information

section-54-1.TO: ensure that arrangements are in force for securing that any material obtained under the warrant is handed over to overseas authorities
section-54-1.ONLY IF: the requirements of subsection (2) are met
section-54-1.IN RELATION TO: every targeted interception warrant or mutual assistance warrant issued by that authority

section-54-1.TO: ensure that arrangements are in force for securing that copies of any such material are given to overseas authorities
section-54-1.IN RELATION TO: every targeted interception warrant or mutual assistance warrant issued by that authority

section-55-2.FOR: The person to whom the warrant is addressed
section-55-2.TO: inform the Investigatory Powers Commissioner of the retention of the item

section-55-3.TO: — (a) direct that the item is destroyed, or (b) impose one or more conditions as to the use or retention of that item
section-55-3.UNLESS: the Commissioner considers that subsection (5) applies to the item

section-55-4.TO: impose such conditions under subsection (3)(b) as the Commissioner considers necessary for the purpose of protecting the public interest in the confidentiality of items subject to legal privilege
section-55-4.IF: the Commissioner considers that subsection (5) applies to the item

section-55-6.TO: require an affected party to make representations about how the Commissioner should exercise any function under subsection (3)
have regard to any such representations made by an affected party (whether or not as a result of a requirement imposed under paragraph (a))

section-57-1.FOR: a person to whom this section applies
section-57-1.TO: make an unauthorised disclosure to another person

section-59-3.TO: show that the person could not reasonably have been expected, after first becoming aware of the matter disclosed, to take steps to prevent the disclosure
section-59-3.IN: proceedings against the person for an offence under this section in respect of any disclosure
